key_insight: A high-dimensional neural network potential can reproduce DFT-level energetics and structure in martensitic NiTi, enabling realistic finite-temperature simulation of phase behavior.
engineering_relevance: This gives a fast atomistic surrogate for studying shape-memory alloy deformation, twinning, and thermal evolution at scales far beyond direct DFT.
method: Trained an HDNNP on DFT data for NiTi martensite.
Validated against equilibrium structures, elastic constants, stacking-fault energies, and vibrational spectra.
Used molecular dynamics to probe temperature-driven structural evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate agreement with DFT, including subtle B19' vs B33 energy differences on the order of meV/atom and an anisotropic stacking-fault energy landscape.
watch_item: Because the model is trained for the martensitic phase, transferability to other NiTi phases, defects, or chemistries may require additional validation.
paper_title: A high-dimensional neural network potential for finite-temperature phenomena in NiTi martensite
